questions.text: State the unit of the surface tension coefficient.
In what unit is the surface tension coefficient expressed?

The movable wire of a wire frame is 5 cm long, and the soap film is stretched by 10 cm. Find the magnitude of the stretching force (mN). The surface tension coefficient of the soap solution is 40 mN/m.
Find the mass (mg) of a water drop falling from a capillary tube 4 mm in diameter. σ = 73 mN/m.
A water drop detached from a vertical glass tube 1 mm in diameter. What is the weight of the drop (mN)? The surface tension coefficient of water is σ = 73 mN/m.
Water drips from a tube 1.8 mm in diameter. How many drops are there in 1 cm³ of water? The surface tension coefficient of water is σ = 72 mN/m.
Kerosene drops fall one per second from a dropper with an orifice 2.0 mm in diameter. How long (min) does it take for 25 cm³ of kerosene to flow out? ρ = 800 kg/m³, σ = 24 mN/m.
A liquid of mass 100 g with a surface tension coefficient of 50 mN/m drips from a dropper of radius half a millimeter. How many drops does it form?
Find the mass (mg) of a water drop detached from a dropper 1 mm in diameter moving downward with an acceleration of 4.5 m/s². σ = 73 mN/m.

Water drips from a tube into a small bath of volume 6 cm³. The inner diameter of the tube is 1.0 mm. How many drops of water must fall from the tube to fill the bath with water at 20°C? ρ = 1000 kg/m³, σ = 72 mN/m.
A dropper with an orifice 2 mm in diameter contains 219 cm³ of water. How many drops will fall from the dropper in total? Take π = 3, g = 10 m/s².
The diameter of a dropper orifice is 1.2 mm. What is the mass (mg) of a water drop flowing out of the dropper at the moment of detachment?
Determine the excess pressure (Pa) produced by the surface of an air bubble 18 mm in diameter under water. σ = 72 mN/m.
Determine the excess pressure (Pa) produced by the surface of a soap bubble 20 mm in diameter. σ = 0.04 N/m.
Calculate the excess potential energy (J) of the surface of a soap bubble 50 mm in diameter. σ = 0.04 N/m.
What is the surface energy (mJ) of a soap bubble of radius 4 cm? σ = 40 mN/m, π = 3.
By what factor must the radius of a soap bubble be increased for its surface energy to increase 64 times?
How much work (mJ) must be done to blow up a soap bubble from a radius of 1 cm to 6 cm? σ = 45 mN/m.
How many microjoules of work must be done to increase the surface area of a soap bubble from 1 cm² to 3 cm²? σ = 5 · 10⁻² N/m.
A water drop of radius 0.6 mm hits a smooth surface and breaks into 8 identical small droplets. What is the minimum height (cm) from which the drop fell? σ = 72 mN/m.
A water drop of radius 0.3 mm hits a smooth surface and breaks into 8 identical small droplets. What is the minimum height (cm) from which the drop fell? σ = 72 mN/m.
Eight spherical mercury droplets at the same temperature merge into a single drop. How does the temperature change in this process, and why?
answers: It increases, because the surface energy increases.
It decreases, because the surface energy decreases.
It rises, because the surface energy decreases.
It does not change, because the surface energy does not change.
